hypothesis: Which profilers work inside the P1 Lambda (python3.12, arm64, 10,240 MB, SnapStart) and what each costs. Each profiler arm runs P1's code with one profiler on; its cost is the difference in Lambda's own REPORT numbers against a REPORT-only control, paired by round (and by request for warm), Graviton3 only. 'nvidia-spi' (the operator's word) is read as NVIDIA's tooling: nvidia-smi and Nsight Systems/Compute.

conclusion: SUPERSEDED by run 20261020T231634Z; overhead conclusions withdrawn. This run reused one Lambda client across sequential version publication and SnapStart waits: 45 restore invokes died as client read timeouts that never reached Lambda (earlier misreported here as a Lambda platform stall), leaving the rep restore control one valid Graviton3 sample in rounds 0, 2 and 4. Its noise floor was the X-Ray arm's own deltas. Its hot-spot tables are kept, now as shares of all recorded samples (buffer_set_tensor 29.9% and rhs_pack 11.7% of init CPU samples, not 35.2% and 13.7%). Applicability findings are unchanged. Deployed profiler package: lkai-prof-build/1 manifest, which does not bind lkaisamp.c, the Telemetry extension or the py-spy wheel to source; provenance is recorded as unverifiable. Applicability (in Lambda): NVIDIA tools (nvidia-smi, nsys, ncu) are INAPPLICABLE because there is no GPU (no /dev/nvidia*, no PCI 0x10de, no driver or libraries; 7 environments, all Graviton3 0xd40). perf, eBPF, ptrace and py-spy --native are DENIED (EPERM; CapEff 0, seccomp filter, perf_event_paranoid 2, no PMU). These WORK: P1 phase timers, REPORT/CloudWatch, X-Ray, the Telemetry API extension, cProfile, py-spy --nonblocking, and an in-process SIGPROF sampler (lkaisamp), which gives native KleidiAI kernel profiles where perf is denied.
